title: Recording in Copenhagen with Little Brother
summary: She recorded for two days' pay of $300 with Little Brother playing; she had taught him "Mighty Tight Woman".

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: How did you happen to make this record in Copenhagen?

They sent me, they sent me to come on a Wednesday -- I think seven weeks, two months. See, I had to go different places to make a record and so Copenhagen, they wanted me to come up there. So I (unintelligible) wouldn't let Little Brother play piano, none of my songs, say, "Sippie, you can't (unintelligible)." "Sippie, you know you can't (unintelligible).
So you had both of them on that record?
Roosevelt -- no, Roosevelt didn't play for me.
Not on the record . No, he played, but he played instrumental and he sang hissself.

And then Little Brother played instrumental and sang songs and then Little Brother played these numbers for me over there, uh-huh. So the man give me $300.00 for that day's work and give Little Brother $300.00 too (inaudible).
Well, why did you play "I'm a Mighty Tight Woman" yourself? Didn't Little Brother know how to play that song?
Oh, no, he (unintelligible). I had learned it to him.

Yeah, I learned it to him, because I can play anything ____. I can play (unintelligible). All I got to do is get the beat, you know. After I sing it to him one time or I play it first and then he play (unintelligible) but he can soon catch the rhythm and play it. So ____ say, "I'm going to make me a song about me and -- keep your mouth shut, don't be advertising your man." But they would tease me (unintelligible) so crazy about my song, you know.

But he say, "Sippie, I'm going to make me a song ____." But he sang a song about (unintelligible) talking about ____. But Buddy makes the same thing (unintelligible) there was none of the songs as good as mine.
